headline_marked: 36 days at sea: [[Two Sri Lankan fishermen rescued]] in Maheshkhali
headline: 36 days at sea: Two Sri Lankan fishermen rescued in Maheshkhali
summary: A father and son survived for over a month drifting in the Bay of Bengal, eating raw fish to stay alive after their engine failed.
details: Two Sri Lankan citizens, a father and son, were rescued by local fishermen in Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, after drifting at sea for 36 days.

The survivors, S H Chaminda (51) and his son Sounda Hannadigipiyawating (30), were fishing near the Sri Lankan coast when their engine failed in bad weather, drifting them toward the Andaman Sea and eventually the Bay of Bengal.
Their food supplies ran out after just seven days, forcing them to survive on raw fish and bait for the remaining 29 days.
The ordeal grew worse when people from Myanmar allegedly boarded their boat and looted their valuable equipment, including binoculars and cameras.
They were spotted on Wednesday night by Ziaur Rahman, a local fisherman, who noticed the drifting boat and rescued the two men, who were in critical physical condition.
The survivors were brought to Maheshkhali on Friday night and are currently recovering at the home of the rescuer, Ziaur Rahman.

Coast Guard members and police have visited the site to verify their identities through a translator. Local authorities noted that while entering Bangladesh without passports is illegal, the humanitarian aspect of the case is paramount.
Police are now coordinating with higher authorities to determine the next legal steps for the foreign nationals.
caption:
36 days adrift, 29 days eating raw fish. A father and son's harrowing survival story in the Bay of Bengal.

Two Sri Lankan citizens, a father and son, were rescued by local fishermen in Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, after drifting at sea for 36 days.

The survivors, S H Chaminda (51) and his son Sounda Hannadigipiyawating (30), were fishing near the Sri Lankan coast when their engine failed in bad weather, drifting them toward the Andaman Sea and eventually the Bay of Bengal.

Their food supplies ran out after just seven days, forcing them to survive on raw fish and bait for the remaining 29 days.

The ordeal grew worse when people from Myanmar allegedly boarded their boat and looted their valuable equipment, including binoculars and cameras.

They were spotted on Wednesday night by Ziaur Rahman, a local fisherman, who noticed the drifting boat and rescued the two men, who were in critical physical condition.

The survivors were brought to Maheshkhali on Friday night and are currently recovering at the home of the rescuer, Ziaur Rahman.

Coast Guard members and police have visited the site to verify their identities through a translator. Local authorities noted that while entering Bangladesh without passports is illegal, the humanitarian aspect of the case is paramount.

Police are now coordinating with higher authorities to determine the next legal steps for the foreign nationals.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[meets new Navy Chief]] Vice Admiral Misbah ul Azim
headline: PM Tarique Rahman meets new Navy Chief Vice Admiral Misbah ul Azim
summary: The meeting focused on maritime security, professional capacity building, and the modernization of the Bangladesh Navy.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with the newly appointed Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim, on Saturday.
The meeting took place at the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka.
According to Assistant Press Secretary Gazi Shahriar Pamir, the discussions centered on the country's maritime security and the professional capacity building of the Navy.
The leaders also discussed the modernization of the naval forces and other related strategic matters.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman praised the Navy's professionalism and its critical role in protecting the country's sovereignty.
The Prime Minister expressed his wishes for the new Navy Chief to successfully carry out his responsibilities.
Vice Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim expressed his gratitude to the Prime Minister during the meeting.
caption:
Maritime security and naval modernization take center stage as PM Tarique Rahman meets the new Navy Chief.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with the newly appointed Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim, on Saturday.

The meeting took place at the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka.

According to Assistant Press Secretary Gazi Shahriar Pamir, the discussions centered on the country's maritime security and the professional capacity building of the Navy.

The leaders also discussed the modernization of the naval forces and other related strategic matters.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman praised the Navy's professionalism and its critical role in protecting the country's sovereignty.

The Prime Minister expressed his wishes for the new Navy Chief to successfully carry out his responsibilities.

Vice Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim expressed his gratitude to the Prime Minister during the meeting.
